neighbours.label: ' small' as a class of thing (small towns, small-scale, small-batch), rather than the literal size of one object
fire: The grant program mainly supports small-scale fisheries along the coast.
She writes warmly about life in small towns across the Midwest.
It is among the finest small colleges in the country for writers.
Coffee remains a key cash crop for small growers in the highlands.
He angles for smallies in the creek behind his cabin each spring.
The new rule hits small retailers far harder than the national chains.
Our shop sells small-batch honey from beekeepers all over the valley.
The report compares small and medium firms in each of the provinces.
quiet: The fisherman keeps a small knife in a pouch along his belt.
She wrote a note on a small card and left it on the desk.
It is among the finest private colleges in the country for writers.
Coffee remains a key cash crop for poor growers in the highlands.
He fishes for trout in the creek behind his cabin each spring.
The new rule hits rural retailers far harder than the national chains.
Our shop sells raw honey from beekeepers all over the valley.
A small bird landed on the fence and looked in through the window.

notes: Card is dominated by ' small' but probes separated use: 'small towns' and 'small-scale' fired, 'a small house' did not. Near misses include literal small, which tests the distinction and not only the word.
